#2007. Fulham 1 Newcastle 1 match ratings and comments on all Newcastle United players

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

We asked Dave Marshall to give us his match ratings and comments on individual Newcastle United players after Fulham 1 Newcastle 1.

Nail-biting. Teeth gnashing. Unease. Anxiety. Growing disapproval. Such were the rumblings of a sizable, and growing, section of Newcastle supporters as United headed to west London for a date with Fulham.

The Cottagers a side going in just two points above relegation but showing signs of life in recent weeks.

A good omen for United going in, though: winning three on the bounce in the capital this season with no goals conceded.

But pressure mounting on Matthias Jaissle and the lads after a string of bad results.

While there are both positives and negatives to take from this performance and result v Fulham…

What’s most concerning is the vibe around the club.

It was noticeable Monday at St. James’ Park. And the ranting and raving online has reached ridiculous levels of theatre.

It was good that Newcastle had an away match after capitulating twice to the Merseyside Mackems because St. James’ Park would have been too toxic to have been any support for the black and white today.

This is not the place to debate Jaissle’s tenure or his seemingly increasingly tenuous position to remain United’s gaffer.

This is not the place to criticise the personnel decisions the brass have made in recent months.

Nor is to call out any players for lack of effort, skill, finishing, passing, common sense, etc.

But it is a place to remind you that we are Newcastle United.

And United supporters have a reputation for being among the most loyal, fervent, rabid, and supportive.

50,000 strong showed up on the regular even when having to endure seasons in the Championship.

Traveling Geordies are always lauded, especially on the continent. It’s no stretch to say that a lot of club brass around England are envious of the support Newcastle gets. Supporters who bleed black-and-white.

Think 50,000 would regularly show up if one of the Septics got relegated after so many years without any trophies and Mike Ashley the club owner?

(It’s still early, but we’re on course to find out next season… but I digress.)

Face it… this is nothing compared to the dark ages of the Fat Tub of Ashley years.

The struggles of a team that lost three of its top skill players and several of its top leaders and mostly replaced them with younger, greener, and arguably less-skilled footballers?

Not the worst times United supporters have ever endured.

The learning curve of a new gaffer who’s not been on the touchline even three months yet?

Not the worst depths Geordies have suffered through.

A string of bad performances, bad results, erratic play, defensive mishaps, poor finishing in front of the net…

Not happy with MJ’s tactics or his line-ups or his substitutions or his in-game management?

But what sucks more is the vibe of the supporters right now.

It’s as if a sizable portion of the fanbase is already certain that Matthias Jaissle is a failure and this team is not worthy of support.

The schedule ramps up in quality and intensity after this international break.

So it’s time for us as United supporters to ramp up our own intensity, passion, love, and support for the black-and-white.

Come matchday, it’s time to strap on our favourite United top and do nothing but get behind the team 100%.

When the season kicked off on August 23 at home to Liverpool, pretty much no one expected United to be on 12 points and hovering mid-table after Matchday 10.

Newcastle were tagged for relegation and left for Championship dead. So it’s fair to say that United have exceeded expectations so far.

It’s also easy to forget during a long season, particularly in the midst of a spell of bad results.

Anfield and Old Trafford get all the plaudits for being difficult venues for opponents.

But those of us who live and breathe English football know, even objectively, that no set of supporters gives its team that vital push more than the rabid throngs inside a pulsating St. James’ Park.

And that’s what we have to be again to get through this.

Lukas Hornicek – 8 Bounced back after the flub v Everton on Monday. Stood tall with five saves, several of them spectacular, including early on to deny Oscar Bobb and then a last-second stop to deny Sessegnon’s laserbolt in stoppage time. Can’t be faulted on the equaliser; nothing to be done once it deflected off BDB.

Amar Dedic – 6.5 While he seemed to handle Iwobi, he struggled with Robinson’s overlapping runs. Solid in the first half as United sat back, but lagged as the match went on, his 92nd-minute yellow card invited unnecessary pressure as the draw played out.

Malick Thiaw – 7 Much-needed athleticism was back on the backline. Composed, accurate for most of his time on the pitch. Didn’t clear the ball well enough in the build up to the equaliser.

Dan Burn – 6.5 Goal disallowed due to a soft foul by Wissa. Dominant in the air, and though unlucky for Muniz’s poke to deflect off him for the equaliser, not quick enough to close down the cross that led to it. Solid partnership with Thiaw.

Lewis Hall – 7 As good as we all think Hall to be, and no doubt we’re correct, to be truly world class, he’s got to bury that 88th-minute effort, even with his non-dominant right foot. Back to his usual level for the most part, otherwise.

Sean Steur – 6.5 Good to see him back and playing with confidence. Was tidy on the ball and always looking to direct passes forward. Still not sure about him being part of a two-man midfield. Not really sure about it generally speaking, to be fair.

Nico Gonzalez – 6 Had his moments in the middle of the park, but wonder about his fitness, as he was subbed for the 2nd game in a row on the hour mark. Though he helped United keep their shape, there was no creativity to his game to break down Fulham’s low block.

Yoane Wissa – 5 Will be aggrieved with the soft foul he got called for that cancelled Burn’s would-be goal. Still, can’t put himself in position for such a call. Had a couple of opportunities but made a meal of them. Didn’t trouble the GK as much as he should have.

Jacob Murphy – 8 A screaming curler that should’ve won it and was denied an assist for Burn’s header. A Murphinho performance that United needs more consistently from him, as he was Newcastle’s most consistent threat on the break.

Harvey Barnes – 6.5 Harsh? Maybe. But when you’re an “all-he-does-is-score” kind of footballer, you’ve got to put away at least one of the three glaring chances he didn’t. He caused Fulham all types of issues but not scoring is unforgivable and it cost United two points.

William Osula – 5 Was not the beneficiary of much good service but his inconsistent effort was disappointing, Did not get a shot on goal.

Lewis Miley – 6 Came on for Nico on 61’, vital defensive header to clear a dangerous Iwobi free-kick late but hope competition with Steur will have him passing more forward. Still, good to see him back.

Joe Willock – 6 On for Wissa on 61’, he added energy dynamism to the midfield but only managed 1 SOG, and it was from long range, not too troublesome.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo – 5 On for Steur on 74’, back for the first time in weeks. Late header was saved but not too much impact. Seemed to suffer a knock in stoppage time, so hope it’s not too serious.

Anthony Elanga – N/A (On too late to rate) On for Osula on 85’, no impact in this cameo.

Fabian Schar – N/A (On too late to rate) On for Thiaw on 85’ following the equaliser to help see things out.

Matthias Jaissle – 6 Not sure that this match set-up worked, not with our cast of characters. However, Jaissle’s plan to sit deep and counter was not a bad idea, given the past couple of weeks. A sniff of desperation? Not sure, but it almost worked perfectly. However, another failure to hold the lead. You can blame MJ all you want, but it was the same last season under Howe, and with a much different cast. It’s hard to explain. But it’s got to be fixed.

#2006. “Erased” – Media explanation for one star’s waning at West Ham United

West Ham’s Nuno- divided squad was rallied midweek by new manager Scott Parker with his declaration that the slate had been wiped clean and that everyone had a chance to impress. Indeed as if to prove the point his first match day squad included Soungoutou Magassa, one of the summer want-aways who didn’t get his way.

Although the French midfielder was understandably rusty and hooked at half time, Parker had proved his point. Images of the head coach in training alongside-even- Maxi Cornet showed nobody is beyond redemption in the Coach’s search for the right eleven.

However, anxious voices across the Atlantic continue to berate West Ham for ruining the career of Mexico’s national team captain Edson Alvarez.

Few in Central America seem able to understand el Machin’s fall from grace, despite both injury and scandal dogging the midfielder during the summer. Rather than accepting that the West Ham management simply don’t rate their skipper, the understandably patriotic local media indulge themselves in all manner of excuses for their star’s waning in east London.

Edson Alvarez pictured back in training in Parker’s pre-Blackburn session.

As futnsoccer.com report, the Mexican football sites are claiming he’s been rendered virtually invisible by successive managers:

“91 days in oblivion, with Alvarez still erased from West Ham.

Hispanic Post went further, arguing in an opinion piece that the exclusion points to a deep fracture between the player and the London club’s project.”

I’d suggest after yesterday’s desperate effort without Edson anywhere near the squad, there might be one or two who started the game against Blackburn who might find their positions coming under scrutiny in the next two weeks as Parker gets to grips with the challenge he faces implanting some spine into his chosen line up.

Whereas the first two sides picked may well have been a ‘committee’ selection involving his coaching team, since the new manager only rocked up on Wednesday, two weeks with virtually his whole squad including the likes of Magassa and Alvarez will allow Parker to judge for himself who has the cojones to give his West Ham line up some much-needed moral fibre.

Should Alvarez still not feature, then the Mexican media will simply have to drop the conspiracy theories and face the fact that successive West Ham managers just don’t think he’s good enough for second tier English football.

#2005. The 6 Newcastle United players that can take NUFC forward…in the forward positions

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

It has been tough for many Newcastle United players this season.

Newcastle United players that are new to the club and in so many cases, new to the country and the Premier League.

Throw in the fact United have experienced more injuries this season than any other Premier League club and it adds another level.

It has been a tough watch at times for us as fans but I think as the season goes on, we can see a much better team and season develop.

There has been no continuity, largely down to the injuries, plus of course a manager still finding his feet after arriving only 18 days before the season started and a squad of Newcastle United players that didn’t get a proper run together in pre-season.

My belief is that as the season develops these six Newcastle United players can take NUFC forward, in the forward positions…of midfield and attack:

20 Lewis Miley 18 Sean Steur 24 Nico Gonzalez 20 Bazoumana Toure 21 Matias Fernandez-Pardo 23 William Osula

An average of only 21 for this half dozen and Matthias Jaissle has been trying his best to protect the likes of Steur, Toure and MFP.

Osula and Miley have missed so many matches through injury this season and Lewis Miley ending up playing right-back when he has played usually!

Nico Gonzalez is still bedding in and used to playing every match, rarely with the same teammates in midfield!

With time I think MFP and Toure can be big assets.

I will revisit this later in the season as to how this six have got on…

Adam Nagy is looking forward to playing at San Siro in front of a big crowd as he leads Ferencvaros out against AC Milan.

Ferencvaros have every reason to come into this game full of confidence having won each of their three Europa League fixtures so far. Nagy has become a key part of the team already, having joined in the summer window to become the new midfield anchor.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This will not actually be the first time that the 31-year-old midfielder has played against Milan though, and it will be his second meeting with them at San Siro. Nagy has been involved in four games against the Rossoneri, all with Bologna, with one draw and three defeats.

#2003. Exclusive: Insider’s Verdict On ‘Brighton Star To West Ham’ Transfer Claim

One player who was reportedly linked with a move to West Ham United during the summer transfer window was Brighton & Hove Albion winger Amario Cozier-Duberry.

The 21-year-old joined Middlesbrough on a season-long loan after signing a new three-year contract with the Seagulls earlier this summer.

Cozier-Duberry has made an impressive start to life at the Riverside Stadium, registering three goals and five assists in just ten league appearances.

West Ham strengthened their wide options following the departure of Crysencio Summerville, bringing in Edvin Austbø and Manor Solomon. However, as Claret & Hugh can exclusively reveal, reports suggesting the Hammers submitted either a loan or permanent offer for Cozier-Duberry were inaccurate.

When approached for clarification, a trusted transfer source provided a brief but unequivocal response: “Not true.”

West Ham settled on Austbø – and appear to have done pretty well by signing the up and coming young winger

The winger attracted interest from several clubs during the summer, including Rangers, as uncertainty surrounded his future at Brighton following the club’s reported £21 million investment in Zadock Yohanna.

Before joining Middlesbrough, Cozier-Duberry enjoyed an outstanding loan spell with Bolton Wanderers in League One last season. He scored 11 goals and contributed 13 assists, underlining his reputation as one of the country’s most promising young attacking talents.

At West Ham, Manor Solomon has experienced a mixed start to his spell in east London, while Austbø has already chipped in with two goals and two assists despite largely being used as a substitute.

It will be fascinating to see how Cozier-Duberry’s loan campaign at Middlesbrough develops over the course of the season. However, any suggestion that he was close to wearing a claret-and-blue shirt appears to be wide of the mark.

I have been a season ticket holder since the late eighties, so experienced the highs and lows of being a West Ham supporter. I previously wrote for OLAS and have contributed to a number of football publications in the past.

#2002. Newcastle United perspective on Premier League fixtures to play out today (8 November 2026)

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Looking at these Premier League fixtures on Sunday, in this latest round of matches.

Seeing the other games from a Newcastle United perspective.

This tenth round of Premier League fixtures.

There are five Premier League matches today.

They complete this final round of EPL games before heading into the international break

These are the results so far this weekend:

Saturday 7 November Leeds 1 Tottenham 0 Arsenal 1 Hull 0 Fulham 1 Newcastle United 1 Forest 3 Man City 1

As a Newcastle United fan, have a look at these Premier League fixtures on Sunday and have a think about what you’d like to happen and what is most likely in terms of results.

My conclusions and predictions on these Sunday matches:

Brighton are top of the Premier League form table with five wins and one defeat. However, Brentford have only lost one of their last six, even if winning only two of the last half dozen.

Two teams that are good to watch and I think the fact Brighton had a midweek match might help Brentford get a draw.

Liverpool still don’t look convincing this season despite their huge spending in recent times. Losing to an average Fenerbahce team after having led twice, kind of sums them up.

They are though up against a desperate looking Palace who have lost their last three league matches whilst conceding nine goals and scoring none.

Palace did scratch out a 1-0 Carabao Cup win at Fulham recently and I am hoping they might come out battling here on home turf. I hope they might get a point…

Bournemouth have won their last seven in all competitions and will be big favourites today.

Ipswich though have won two of their four home EPL matches and drawn another. I think the Tractor Boys might get at least a point here, maybe even win.

Sunderland look on a one-way ticket to the Championship and I think flat-track bullies Chelsea will help them along their way back to the lower leagues.

Sunderland have picked up one point from their last six EPL matches and were humiliated at home by Dinamo Zagreb in midweek.

I would be very surprised if Chelsea don’t win this by at least a couple.

Man U are in the relegation zone for very good reason. Only a lucky win against Ipswich all season in the Premier League and if Villa turn up today then this will be an away win.

Man U fluked a midweek victory against an average Roma side in midweek but my prediction is that Carrick and his players will enter the international break on the back of another defeat. Whether Carrick is still in charge after the internationals…unlikely.

#2001. West Ham fans’ furious reaction raises an uncomfortable question

As the Hammers subsided to their first away defeat in the Championship, long suffering supporters, who’d undertaken the 480 mile round trip to be served up a pretty spineless team performance, decided to let their team have it with both barrels.

After last week’s displeasure culminating an Hammers fans singing ‘sacked in the morning’ to their own manager, this weekend brought the players into the crosshairs as the next logical target for their ire.

..With Nuno Espirito Santo out of the job and with Scott Parker just 72 hours in, the 7,500+ travelling fans turned on their stars.

Under no illusions after the result – and the away fans’ response – yesterday: Scott Parker

..As well as booing their own goal keeper pretty much throughout, if the reports on the radio were correct.

Traditionalists will likely be aghast at the thought of fans undermining their own team in this manner, whilst those who participated no doubt feel it was the only way to show their contempt for the perceived lack of commitment and effort which those eleven representatives  of the Claret and Blue heritage displayed.

Not to mention the hundreds of pounds it costs each supporter, every game, merely to arrive at the turnstiles in support of our club. But is it the ‘right’ thing to do?

For me – it’s a no. I started attending games with my son when he was ten years old and however bad it got (it was pretty dire in that season of 2003-4) we never left early, never booed our own players (Luis Boa Morte excepted, I must confess to once letting my frustration with his indolence bubble over) and always, always applauded those who’d put in a shift, regardless of outcome. And I’d not even heard ‘you’re not fit to wear the shirt‘ sung by West Ham fans in my couple of decades’ worth of attending games.

I just don’t see it helping team morale or positively influencing the final outcome. Which is, after all, the point of ‘supporters’.

Giving ‘The Sun’ another gleeful headline to point out our sufferings sticks in my throat too.

But don’t get me wrong, each has absolutely the right to their own response. Just don’t see it helping is all.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

To the negatives, support our team or push off. I have attended since 58. We never had the Russian or Mafia money but it is still our club. Great memories of neighbours and friends who played for the club. Most of our players did their best, including youngsters but we need a strong striker and physical keeper.

been trying to get more away tickets, anyone who doesn’t want to go and watch the away games, step aside there’s plenty who want to go but can’t get tickets….

Booing is not motivational we have a new manager who has seemingly had very limited time with the squad he needs a chance to see what he can do and Booing is not helping. The club has had many problems for some time. The situation is frustrating from now on we have to get behind the team.

How can anyone be surprised. Week after week watching the same old dross . A centre back who would struggle to get a game in a pub team and a goalkeeper who is totally useless. Considering how much it costs to travel to, & to get into, games – & the grossly excessive salaries the players receive – I consider that the supporters have every right to criticise what they see from the players on the pitch. It could be counter-productive, in that it upsets the players’ mindsets & effort, but what about the mindsets of those who, at least partially, pay their salaries. I don’t like to see the players get booed etc., but the supporters do have the right to express their opinions – just as they do when they cheer the players. These are professional players & yet they continue to serve up displays which are not even worthy of amateurs – who don’t get paid obscene salaries & do it for the love of the game. They should take the supporters’ criticisms as an incentive to raise their game & make an extra effort for , what could be described as, their employers.

I don’t agree with these chants, but if you are a paying customer, it is your right I suppose. All I will say is, if Scott Parker wasn’t aware of the size of the job he has signed up for, he certainly does now. And when it comes to the goalkeeping situation, Hermandsen reminds me of Mervyn Day, a very good young keeper who came through the youth ranks, which we all really like. But through a series of unfortunate incidents, like being lobbed from forty yards on a couple of occasions, he had been reduced to a rabbit in the headlights, his nerve completely shot. John Lyall realising that in his current state of mind he wouldn’t be good enough to take us forward, did the extremely unkind but completely necessary act of removing him from the team, and go out and break the world record for Phil Parkes, and that didn’t work out to badly did it? Harsh, absolutely, but football doesn’t exist on seniment, difficult choices sometimes have to be made. Mr Parker has been around the game long enough to be well aware of this, and I don’t think he will hesitate to do whatever is required to fix this and other positions.

#2000. After being benched for Celtic loan star, my on-field response was emphatic

Lucas Clearie has issued another reminder of his goalscoring potential after hitting a first-half hat-trick for Celtic B.

The 17-year-old was benched for the midweek KDM Evolution Trophy clash with Ross County, with Shim Mheuka preferred through the middle.

But Clearie responded in emphatic fashion just four days later with a first-half hat-trick against Beith Juniors. The striker opened the scoring in the 18th minute before adding another in the 42nd minute. He completed his hat-trick in the 45th minute.

His latest haul takes Clearie to an impressive 23 goals across Lowland League and KDM Evolution Trophy football this season.

Eighteen of those have arrived in the league, while he has also struck five times in four KDM Evolution Trophy outings. It was Clearie’s second hat-trick of the campaign after he previously scored three in a dramatic 4-3 victory over Stranraer.

Martin O’Neill answers Celtic ‘chucked it’ claims after major team gamble

The ongoing Celtic problem that must be ‘addressed’ in January

Chris Sutton delivers brutal ‘all-inclusive holiday’ jibe at new Celtic star

His prolific form comes as he attempts to force his way into the thoughts of first-team manager Martin O’Neill.

Clearie was among seven Celtic youngsters handed their first professional contracts in the summer of 2025 and has continued to enhance his reputation with the B team.

The teenager’s latest treble also rounded off an impressive week after he was included alongside Celtic teammate Corey Shaw in the Scotland Under-19 squad.

Scotland are due to face Kazakhstan, Kosovo and Belgium during the international window.

#1999. First meeting against a team 20 unbeaten: All the key stats ahead of Milan vs. Ferencvaros

The first ever competitive meeting between AC Milan and Ferencvaros will take place at San Siro this evening in the Europa League.

Milan have played four times in history against Hungarian opponents. The first time was in the 1967-68 Cup Winners’ Cup, when the Rossoneri draw 2-2 away and 1-1 at home against ETO, which saw them progress on away goals.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The other two occasions came 15 years later in the 1982 Mitropa Cup group stage against Szombathelyi Haladas. The Diavolo won both encounters: 2-0 at San Siro, and 1-0 away from home.

So, tonight’s contest is an unprecedented one, and it pits two teams together that have made very different starts to their Europa League campaigns.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has caught the eye for Milan in Europa League play. The striker is the side’s top scorer with three goals, which is joint most in the competition, one of those having been the critical first of the match.

➤ Kristoffer Zachariassen has been the most prolific player for Ferencváros, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied as the competition’s top scorer in 2026-27.

➤ The Rossoneri secured an impressive 3-1 victory over city rivals Inter at the weekend, strengthening their position in the Serie A top-four race. Milan have lost just once in their opening ten league matches, recording six victories and three draws, although their continental performances have been considerably less convincing.

➤ The Diavolo suffered a comprehensive 3-0 defeat away to Bournemouth on matchday three, leaving them with two losses from their opening three Europa League fixtures and only one victory in their last six European matches overall.

➤ Milan’s struggles have extended to home soil, where they lost 2-0 against Benfica in their only previous Europa League fixture at the Giuseppe Meazza this season. Another defeat would see them lose consecutive European home matches within a single campaign for the first time since 2010/11.

➤ Nevertheless, their recent attacking form offers some encouragement: five of their last six competitive matches have produced at least three goals, and Amorim’s side has scored before the 25th minute in each of their previous four home fixtures.

➤ Ferencváros, by contrast, have enjoyed an outstanding start to their European campaign, winning all three league-phase matches and scoring freely along the way. Their most recent outing produced a convincing 4-1 victory over Torreense, with Bamidele Yusuf, Mariano Gómez and Krisztián Lisztes among the scorers. Balázs Borbély’s side have now won five of their last six competitive matches, drawing the other, and have scored 18 goals while conceding just four during that sequence.

➤ The Hungarian champions are unbeaten in 20 competitive matches since late July, recording 13 victories and seven draws, while each of their last four wins has come by at least two goals. They also boast an impressive away record, having avoided defeat in their last ten competitive matches on the road and conceded no more than once in any of those fixtures.

➤ Victory in Milan would see Ferencváros win four consecutive matches in major European competition for the first time since the 1967-68 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup, when they recorded six successive victories on their way to the final.

➤ This will be the first competitive meeting between Milan and Ferencváros, although both clubs have limited historical experience against opposition from the other’s country. Milan’s only previous European encounters with Hungarian opponents came against Győri ETO in the 1967/68 Cup Winners’ Cup, with both matches ending level.

➤ Ferencváros, meanwhile, have failed to win any of their last four European away fixtures against Italian teams, drawing twice and losing twice, since defeating Roma in the 1965 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup. With Milan seeking to revive their European campaign and the visitors determined to preserve their perfect record, both sides have considerable motivation heading into this encounter.

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Fulham fans have commenting before AND after the Newcastle United match at Craven Cottage,

A 1-1 draw yesterday. Interesting to compare and contrast what Fulham fans had to say pre and post-match.

Fulham fans comment via their Friends of Fulham and Fulham Web message boards:

‘I saw this about Newcastle “they have scored just once from their past 47 shots in all competitions.” which always worries me!!!’

‘Hell, we’ve only scored once from our past 40 shots in all competitions!’

‘This really needs to be a win by multiple goals. We’re at home against a struggling team with a manager under fire, and who have had two fewer rest days than us plus have a player suspended.’

I certainly don’t think we will lose this one. If (and it’s a big if) we get our shooting boots on then a win may a good margin is a distinct possibility.’

‘This is the time when we should beat them. If you look at their results so far this season the standout loss is 4-1 to Coventry.’

‘Not that anyone will be really interested, but at one time in my younger days, my neighbour in Worcester Park in Surrey was Charlie Mitten, who was a lovely man. I have a feeling that Bobby Robson moved into the same house when Charlie moved.’

‘Newcastle lost 1-0 at home to Everton and it should have been by a lot more.’

‘Newcastle have some very good players, so whilst they looked disjointed on Monday night, clicking into gear can’t be too far away. Any hint of complacency from our lads and they will get a result.’

‘Need to stick with an unchanged team. Playing some good football at the minute and fancy us to beat Newcastle.’

‘Leno is my MOTM. Without him that’s a painful loss.’

‘Fulham had more possession today, but Newcastle made better use of theirs. We had 58% possession, with 7 shots and only 2 on target, compared with Newcastle’s 42% possession, 9 shots and 5 on target. We were really lucky to come away with a point.’

‘I gave it to Leno who made some tremendous saves which kept us in the game. Newcastle would have won it at the end when Hall was right in front of goal, if it wasn’t for Big Bernt. ‘

‘The bromance between Rob Jones and Dan Burn seems to be blossoming. I’ve never seen a player given so much ref time.’

‘Indeed. Burn was in the ear of the Jones so often, it gave the impression the pair of them must be refereeing the game together.

Credit to Jones however. He didn’t appear to let Burn’s incessant commentary sway him.’

‘Well it was okay I suppose. But two points lost means we have to win them against the odds somewhere else.

Leno absolutely superb (getting better rather than washed up) but motm must go to Muniz for his physical bombardment of the Newcastle defence turned the match.

Unfortunately the best all time Fulham player on show was Dan Burn, no longer the hopeless bandylegs of yore, who skillfully stymied much our play.’

‘Good point, all told. Great performances from both keepers.’

‘Better than defeat but we need to be winning these games.’

‘Could have, and probably should have, won that, but at least we got something from the game. Muniz the biggest positive from this game, he should definitely start in the next one.’

‘I agree on paper, but Newcastle played better than most of us were expecting. They easily had the better chances today. When you go behind while looking like you have the attacking force of a blunt spoon, a rescued point becomes pretty good.’

‘I leave happy with that effort from the team. It could have gone either way. Toon must have thought they had won it and Harvey Barnes was denied his 100th goal as a bonus.’

‘Second week in a row where the oppo keeper is probably their MoTM, we just need a bit more luck and we’ll be fine. We’re restricting teams to minimal chances so if we can’t score at least we’re solid at the back. Few players not at their best today, think Charles was below the standard he set in the first 9 but they’re not robots and it happens. We need to find a way to be a bit quicker at getting it forward, amount of times today GG made a run and no pass came was criminal and whilst I appreciate we want to control the game via possession, I’d risk turning it over a few times to try something different. AA’s subs were correct again today so positives across the board, it’s more annoying that for the first time this season Newcastle decided to revert to bus parking tactics compared to being gun-ho like they did in the first 9.’

‘Battle of the keepers and both teams could have won. Probably a fair result.

I will say it’s getting boring watching teams park the bus against us.’

‘We created some good chances in the second half and were unlucky not to convert more of them. But for all our possession, we still don’t create enough chances or finish enough of the ones we do create. As SerbianLad pointed out in the matchday thread, “Same old story. We dominate the game but are wasteful in the final third, whether it’s poor final ball or poor finishing (or sometimes great GK saves, tbf). Same story for pretty much the entire season so far.”‘

‘But we really didn’t dominate the game. We had more possession, but Newcastle was fine with that. In terms of chances, it was very equal.’

‘I gave Leno a bit of stick earlier in the season, but he has certainly redeemed himself by much improved performances recently, and he will deservedly win MOTM. The save against Lewis Hall at the end make me jump out of my seat. I felt like it was all huff and puff from us today without much end product. A step down from recent performances where we should have scored 5 in each if we could finish at all. Great to see Muniz reinvigorated, and hopefully he can help with that problem going forward. The referee had a good game.’

‘Fair result in the end as really not much in it between both sides. Thought Bassey and Leno were our best players, but a big shoutout to Berge in the first half as he was immense. Iwobi I thought was also very good first half. We started the second half slow and that gave Newcastle a bit more belief; Palacios was great when he came on IMO, as was Muniz.’

‘Two fairly evenly matched teams settled for some dull stuff in the first half and Newcastle came out after the break far perkier than our lads. Draw is a reasonable result under circumstances.

Not sure I learned much new about our team or individuals. Thought I’d sleep on it before posting, perhaps some inspiration would arrive overnight. It hasn’t. Palacios is obviously going to be a fine player, but it’s equally obvious that we are something of a learning experience for him and that pass was a mistake of callow youth.

As an England supporter, Lewis Hall’s performance was a small comfort. #1997. Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang

Mentally liberated and physically rested, Arsenal began the new Premier League campaign with a performance befitting champions. Gone are the anxieties of last season, when the title race gnawed away at their minds and bodies. Gone are the pressures of chasing a first Premier League trophy in more than two decades. Arsenal look slick, refreshed and hungry for more.

“Champions of England, we know what we are,” sang the home supporters in this thrashing of promoted Coventry City. The players moved with the same energy and confidence, as they dominated every aspect of this match against Frank Lampard’s side.

There will, of course, be many tougher games than this one over the course of the season. But there can be no doubt that Arsenal are settled and strong. Everywhere Coventry looked, they saw world-class opponents who knew exactly what to do and where to be. This was Coventry’s first Premier League match since 2001 and it was a reminder, as if one was needed, of the size of the gulf between England’s top two divisions. Thankfully for Lampard, his season will not be decided by matches against teams of Arsenal’s quality.

As it was in last weekend’s Community Shield victory over Manchester City, Mikel Arteta’s side purred and flowed in attack. The rejuvenated Martin Odegaard scored again, as did his close friend Kai Havertz. Bukayo Saka also struck, easing any lingering concerns about his fitness. Both Saka and Declan Rice, who endured such draining campaigns last year, looked sharp.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

There was also another promising performance by new signing Christos Tzolis, while midfield dynamo Myles Lewis-Skelly continued where he left off at the end of last season: winning tackles, spinning past opponents and firing up the home crowd. New face Bruno Guimarães, absent through injury for a few days, was certainly not needed here.

“They know how to do it,” Arteta said of his players. “They know what they have to do. There was a lot to like in the performance. The manner we started the game, with such domination, clarity, understanding and flow, it was really impressive. At this level the players have to be decisive. They were certainly decisive today.”

Coventry had attempted to irritate Arsenal with physicality and direct passes, but it never looked likely to work, despite the best efforts of strikers Ellis Sims and Taiwo Awoniyi. They will not be the first team to struggle against Arsenal’s defenders, and this will not be the first occasion in which their goalkeeper Carl Rushworth is kept busy.

“Arsenal were the best team in the league last year and they showed it,” Lampard said. “They played like it. The noise here at the start of the game, it was different. I remember that noise. It’s different to the Championship.”

"They played like champions" 🏆Frank Lampard said Coventry will learn lessons after their 3-0 opening day defeat to Arsenal ❌ pic.twitter.com/wqA2kngUVt

Before this opening match, Arteta had objected to the idea that Arsenal were planning to “defend” their title. Instead, he said, they are going to “attack” the Premier League once again. It was a classic Arteta-ism, but the manager’s meaning was clear: he wants his team to be aggressive, inventive and courageous. Perhaps more so than in the second half of last season, when their defending was a greater strength than their attacking.

If that was a case of Arteta talking the talk, then his players happily followed it up by walking the walk here. Arsenal played with an unmistakable swagger, as if they simply knew there would only be one outcome against a group of Coventry players with limited experience at this level.

The energy of the home supporters, as buoyant as you might expect following last season’s triumph, undoubtedly helped Arsenal. There were none of the nerves that defined the run-in in the spring, with the fans instead in a partying mood from the moment new signing Ezri Konsa was introduced to the Emirates Stadium before kick-off.

The opening goal took only 15 minutes to arrive, as Havertz swept in an accurate finish from Riccardo Calafiori’s low cross. It has been a good summer for Havertz, who missed so much of last season with injury but has found some rhythm over the past few months. Including friendlies and his performances for Germany at the World Cup, this was his 10th goal in his last 17 appearances.

Coventry have invested in some powerful, commanding players this summer, but there were signs that the physical battle was proving difficult for Lampard’s side. Caleb Yirenkyi is their new club-record signing in midfield, but he was brutally thrown to the floor by Lewis-Skelly in the first half.

Saka’s goal was the result of a quick cross by Tzolis, the new £34m winger who has made such an exciting start to his Arsenal career. The Greek forward was the star of the first half, constantly making things happen, and his delivery was diverted into Saka’s path after 23 minutes.

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Odegaard showed in the Community Shield that he is in a more confident place than the last campaign, when he constantly battled injuries, and his early-season form continued here. His goal was scruffy, bobbled in off the right foot, but his all-round performance was typically smooth. With two goals in two games, he has already beaten his tally from last season.

"It's a top finish I would say" 😂Martin Odegaard reacts to his goal against Coventry! pic.twitter.com/mciFfZ6Fhx

From there, the game was over. Arsenal could remove Saka, Rice and Odegaard, safe in the knowledge that their work was done. A comfortable night for the champions, and the perfect start.

"How are you going to keep everyone happy? Winning." 🔥Mikel Arteta reveals his secret for keeping his full squad content after Arsenal's 3-0 win against Coventry 👀 pic.twitter.com/IarLijhd6I

"I think we can do even better to be fair" Martin Odegaard reflects on Arsenal's win over Coventry in the first game of the season 💭 pic.twitter.com/nB2YW83VlE

It’s all over in the capital and Arsenal have started their reign as Premier League champions with a confident and assured three-goal victory over newly-promoted Coventry. Havertz, Saka and Odegaard were all on target in a flawless team performance from Arteta’s men. It’s been a tough evening for Lampard’s side, who simply couldn’t handle Arsenal.

FULL-TIME: Arsenal cruise to victory against Coventry on the opening day of the new season! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/ctybTEor9J

There will be four minutes of added time to round this game off. Merino shoots from long range and aims for the bottom corner, but Rushworth dives to his left and makes the stop.

Awoniyi tries to make a run in behind Arsenal’s defence and latch onto Hamer’s pass. The striker is hauled to the ground by Mosquera, who is lucky to escape a booking. The resulting delivery is smacked straight out of play by Torp. That is such a disappointing cross.

Torp swings a cross into Rudoni, who makes a run from deep. Rudoni meets the delivery, but his glancing header is straight at Raya. It’s Coventry’s best chance of the match but they’ve failed to convert it. Arsenal’s clean sheet remains intact.

Arteta makes his fifth and final substitution as Calafiori, who recorded the assist for Arsenal’s opener, is withdrawn for Hincapie.

Lampard responds with his own alteration, bringing Hamer on for Tchaouna.

Coventry are still waiting for their first shot on target this evening. Arsenal are seeing this game out with exemplary professionalism.

Odegaard and Tzolis are the next players to leave the field. Eze and World Cup winner Merino are on as their replacements. Arteta’s substitutions tonight have underlined Arsenal’s tremendous squad depth, and that is without the involvement of both Guimaraes and Konsa.

Lewis-Skelly tries to slide a pinpoint pass through to Calafiori, in an attempt to recreate Arsenal’s opening goal from their Community Shield triumph. It nutmegs Torp, but Rushworth makes a quick dash off his line to collect the ball and eliminate any danger.

Lampard adds some fresh legs and orders a double change. Awoniyi, who makes his Coventry debut, and Rudoni are on, with Simms and Thomas-Asante taken off.

Here come some Arsenal changes. Rice and Saka depart to loud ovations, with Zubimendi and Madueke on to replace them.

Tzolis motors into the Coventry penalty area once again and picks out Havertz, who makes a intelligent run across the six-yard box. Before he can cross or shoot, Thomas sprints over to make an interception.

The visitors then fail to clear a corner and Tzolis slams a low, powerful effort at goal. Rushworth gets down low and spills it, but Thomas is there to hack it away.

Lampard makes the first change of the match for either side as Torp replaces Yirenkyi, whose endured a difficult debut in central midfield for his new side.

Odegaard is enjoying himself out there this evening. Just as he did against Manchester City, he’s playing with such authority, purpose and confidence.

The ball breaks to Tzolis who unleashes a venomous effort at goal. It takes a big deflection and flies out for a corner.

From a Coventry corner, Arsenal counter attack with such intensity and speed. The move ends as Odegaard attempts to find Tzolis with a through ball, but the Norwegian overhits the pass and delayed it too long. The offside flag is then raised against Tzolis.

Van Ewijk attempts to find Simms with a chipped cross towards the back post, but it’s marginally over the striker’s head as Coventry step up their search to pull a goal back.

It’s a nightmare start to the second half for Coventry. Whatever Arteta said to his players at the break has worked wonders.

Lewis-Skelly then shoots from long range and his shot is tipped over the bar by Rushworth.

White overlaps Saka and latches onto the winger’s pass. Saka then tees up Odegaard, who scuffs his close-range effort. Rushworth is wrong-footed and despite getting a glove to it, the ball trickles into the net and Arsenal are cruising.

It's Martin Odegaard... Arsenal have three! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/LrqSSGJWE6

Odegaard has scored some beautiful goals in an Arsenal shirt. That wasn’t one of them. He won’t care, though. Two goals in two games for the Arsenal captain.

Read more about his return to form here: https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2026/08/21/odegaard-a-man-possessed-in-bid-to-unlock-arsenal-attack/

We are back under way for the second half. Will Arsenal add more goals to their tally or can Coventry produce a memorable comeback?

It’s been a steep learning curve for the newly-promoted side, who have been overpowered and outclassed by Arsenal’s quality.

Arsenal are in complete control thanks to a commanding first half display against Coventry. Havertz and Saka have the goals, with the reigning Premier League champions on course to claim a routine three points to kickstart their title defence.

Once again, Saka plays a short corner. Odegaard then passes to Rice, who is in acres of space on the edge of the penalty area. The midfielder shoots, but his curling effort drifts narrowly wide of the far post.

There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.

The ball bobbles into Tchaouna’s path and the winger tries a very ambitious acrobatic effort from the edge of the box. It had Raya worried for a second, but the effort lands on the roof of the net. That would have been a spectacular goal if it had sneaked in.

Tzolis teases Thomas and works some space before clipping a cross in towards Havertz. The forward doesn’t connect with the header and Coventry scramble it clear.

Odegaard is pulling the strings and slips a delightful pass through to the onrushing White, who finds himself very far forward, but the right back is swiftly closed down by Coventry’s defence as he shoots.

At the other end, Simms does brilliantly to turn Gabriel and win a free kick just outside the box. The Brazilian centre back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

Coventry are feeling the full effects of the stark difference in levels between Championship and Premier League. Arsenal look streets ahead at the moment.

Christos Tzolis has only played a few games for Arsenal but it’s already easy to see why he registered 29 assists for Club Brugge last season. He has shown on numerous occasions this summer that he is willing to cross the ball as soon as he receives it. No delay, no faff. It worked against Manchester City last weekend and it created Saka’s goal here.

Welcome back to the Premier League, Coventry... It’s been a chastening opening 27 minutes for Lampard’s side.

Yirenkyi then receives a yellow card on his debut for pulling Lewis-Skelly’s shirt.

Rice strides through midfield and plays a one-two with Odegaard. The English midfielder tees up Tzolis, whose fires a cross into the corridor of uncertainty. Rushworth parries it into the danger zone, gifting an unmarked Saka a simple finish from close range. What a start for the champions!

"Saka couldn't miss!"Arsenal are cruising against Coventry as Bukayo Saka fires home from close range 💥 pic.twitter.com/er411Bi1wh

Arsenal are purring and oozing confidence. Coventry need to be careful and must stay in this game. They cannot allow Arsenal to get a second and run away with this.

Coventry had started well but their first error in defence was ruthlessly punished. That’s Havertz’s 10th goal in his last 17 matches for club and country (including pre-season friendlies). After such an injury-disrupted campaign last year, he’s had a very good summer.

Van Ewijk fails to clear his lines and he’s closed down by Tzolis. The ball ricochets into Calafiori’s path and the left back picks out Havertz with a low cross.

The German sweeps a composed shot into the bottom corner. It’s such a cultured finish and Arsenal begin their defence of the Premier League with a 1-0 lead after 15 minutes.

"The champions are on their way!" Kai Havertz sweeps home from the edge of the box to give Arsenal an early lead against Coventry 👏 pic.twitter.com/SNtrMSPkYJ

Some steady possession for Coventry, who are looking to take the sting and excitement out of the game while also calming the buoyant Arsenal fans down.

Tzolis pops up on the right wing and latches onto Rice’s pass. The attacker then delivers a first-time cross into the box which finds Saka, whose half-volley is blocked by Amenda.

Arsenal then work a short corner that ends with White teeing up Tzolis, but his low strike is smothered by Coventry’s defence. Tzolis has certainly made a lively start, and unsurprisingly, Arsenal’s set pieces are causing some early problems.

Tzolis looks dangerous as he dribbles at Van Ewijk, before cutting inside and unleashing a powerful shot. However, his effort is high and wide. Nevertheless, it’s positive play from Arsenal’s new signing.

Following that Coventry corner, the Premier League holders have monopolised the possession in the early minutes. Chants of ‘Champions of England, we know what we are’ ring around the stadium thanks to the home support, who are in full voice.

Coventry get us under way and the newly-promoted side have won an early corner, which is comfortably dealt with by Arsenal’s defence.

The atmosphere at the Emirates is electric. Can Arsenal flex their title-winning credentials once again or will Coventry cause an almighty upset?

New Arsenal signing Ezri Konsa has been presented on the pitch, with both sets of players set to follow him any moment now.

The 2026-27 season is just minutes away from kicking off.

Coventry have recruited some powerful, aggressive players this summer. They will be looking to frustrate Arsenal by shutting down the spaces around their penalty area, and they will certainly be competitive at set-pieces.

Meanwhile, the Arsenal fans have just had their first glimpse of Ezri Konsa in the club’s shirt. The new signing walked out onto the pitch to wave to the supporters.

With just over five minutes until the 2026-27 Premier League season starts, here are tonight’s teams in full...

Arsenal: Raya, White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori, Odegaard, Rice, Lewis-Skelly, Saka, Havertz, Tzolis.

Subs: Arrizabalaga, Hincapie, Eze, Gyokeres, Madueke, Nwaneri, Merino, Zubimendi, Dowman.

Coventry: Rushworth, van Ewijk, Thomas, Amenda, Dasilva, Onyeka, Yirenkyi, Grimes, Thomas-Asante, Simms, Tchaouna.

Subs: Wilson, Rudoni, Sakamoto, Awoniyi, Kitching, Latibeaudiere, Eccles, Overgaard, Hamer.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Arsenal boss said: “He had a slight tension in his groin. He hasn’t done a pre-season, he only had four or five days before that [Man City] game. We have to take a lot of new stuff for him as well. We need to take it bit by bit.”

Another game, another snub for Gabriel Martinelli. As was the case against Manchester City in last weekend’s Community Shield, the Brazilian isn’t even on the bench tonight. It’s quite clear what’s going on here: Arsenal need to make sales and he is an obvious candidate to depart. It’s not particularly pleasant, though, and you can’t help but feel for a player who has been so important to this club over the last seven years.

Martinelli has made it clear he does not want to move to Galatasary, who made an offer recently. Will a more suitable club come forward for him? We’ll find out in the coming days.

In two full seasons at Coventry between 2021 and 2023, Viktor Gyokeres scored 40 goals in 97 games for Coventry, and was part of the side that lost on penalties to Luton Town in the Championship play-off final to Luton Town.

If Coventry had won that game, would Gyokeres still be wearing a sky blue shirt instead of joining Sporting CP and then Arsenal, who knows...

The striker will have to wait to get onto the pitch against his former team, with Mikel Arteta choosing Kai Havertz to lead the line.

Odegaard comes into the new Premier League season, which begins when Arsenal host Coventry City on Friday night, with a point to prove. That may sound unusual, given his new-found status as a title-winning captain, but last year was a strange one for the 27-year-old. The club’s most successful campaign of his time at Arsenal was also the most frustrating one for Odegaard as an individual.

Last season, Arsenal clinched a much-anticipated Premier League title for the first time in 22 years and are the favourites to lift the trophy for a second successive season. Mikel Arteta’s side have recently claimed the Community Shield and look like they mean business.

Arsenal are clearly not resting on their laurels in their bid to win another top-flight title, having strengthened their squad this summer with the signings of Bruno Guimarães, Christos Tzolis and Ezri Konsa.

Arteta looks raring to go and ready to mount another title charge.

"Everything has to start with me" 💪Mikel Arteta says Arsenal are ready for the new Premier League season 💥 pic.twitter.com/rsUcs7ot7T

After last season’s Championship by a whopping 95 points under Frank Lampard’s management, Coventry head into their first Premier League campaign since suffering relegation from the competition in 2001.

Coventry were playing in the fourth tier as recently as 2017, so lining up against the Premier League holders is a full-circle moment for the club and supporters that is richly deserved.

"I loved it, I loved driving here, feeling the atmosphere, the fans" Frank Lampard on what tonight means for him and Coventry 😍Watch live here: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/077Bga2Z4W

On Friday night, at the home of champions Arsenal, Coventry officially begin a new chapter back in the Premier League and expectations will be high. The man responsible for that tidal wave of optimism is Lampard, their promotion hero.

He has proved a transformative appointment since arriving in November 2024, and the former England and Chelsea captain is relishing the chance to rattle some cages.

His return is a feel-good story and Lampard has a point to prove. He admits that the desire to upset his detractors drives him on. “I’ve got experience of the Premier League and hopefully I can get that across to the players,” he said.

“The club has been out of this division for 25 years so of course it’s exciting. We want to challenge and we want to do well. I’m pleased that we’re here and you want to work at the top. We’re very focused on the job.”

Arsenal ruined Enzo Maresca’s first competitive outing as Man City’s new manager in the club’s first match without Pep Guardiola. It was one-way traffic as Arsenal cruised to a resounding 3-0 win to lift the Community Shield in Cardiff.

Riccardo Calafiori opened the scoring just 23 seconds after he was brilliantly played in by Myles Lewis-Skelly’s defence-splitting pass. Arsenal doubled their lead before the half-hour mark through Kai Havertz’s close-range header and Martin Odegaard added a sumptuously taken third shortly after the interval.

The Premier League holders were in a ruthless mood and completely overran their opponents. Christos Tzolis grabbed two assists out on the left wing, Bruno Guimarães produced a typically commanding performance in the first half and Odegaard controlled proceedings with his creativity.

It was an early taste of silverware for Mikel Arteta’s men, who are the overwhelming favourites to retain their Premier League crown.

"I'm really pleased, that's a really good team" Ian Wright is happy with the Arsenal starting XI to face Coventry, do you agree? 💬 Watch live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/IUBlMS963w

New signings Aurele Amenda, Loum Tchaouna and Caleb Yirenkyi all start and make their Coventry debuts this evening.

Carl Rushworth and Frank Onyeka also begin from the outset after making their moves permanent following successful loans last season.

Your City tonight. 📋 pic.twitter.com/V0nzaemLYF

As Sam Dean confirmed earlier on, Bruno Guimaraes is absent from the squad. The Brazilian was subbed off at half-time in the dominant Community Shield victory over Manchester City with a thigh issue.

Both Declan Rice and Bukayo Saka start after being used off the bench in the Community Shield last weekend, with Guimaraes and Noni Madueke dropping to the bench.

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️Your Premier League opening day XI ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/yRf2BEs3BA

To soften the blow of Bruno Guimaraes’ absence from tonight’s squad due to injury, the Premier League holders can rejoice over the signing of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa for over £50m.

The centre back has penned a four-year deal with the option of a further year.

Speaking to Arsenal’s official website, Sporting Director Andrea Berta said: “Ezri is a defender of high quality, whose athleticism, composure and tactical intelligence have established him as one of the Premier League’s most consistent performers.

“Being comfortable in both central defence and at right-back, Ezri will bring valuable versatility to our squad while maintaining the high defensive standards which are fundamental to our challenge of winning major trophies.”

Konsa will play no role in tonight’s encounter, having only completed the move earlier in the day.

Reinforcing the backline ✍️ pic.twitter.com/deYQhZcmOy

Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

#1996. “He’s Got The Yips” Mads Hermansen’s West Ham Nightmare Goes Beyond Bad Form

There is a phenomenon in sport known as the yips. It’s a condition which seems to affect previously capable sportsmen, psychologically blocking them from performing even the simplest of tasks. In darts, it can become difficult to release the dart from the hand, while in golf it can make putting almost impossible.

In essence, you’re frozen, seemingly unable to perform a task which should have become second nature. And it was during Blackburn Rovers’ second goal against West Ham yesterday, when I watched Mads Hermansen fail to dive, that I found myself wondering whether this goalkeeper has developed the footballing equivalent of the yips.

It wasn’t just that goal, of course. The first was equally concerning, when Ezra Mayers was beaten down the flank and the ball was crossed into the penalty area. The situation required some kind of intervention from Hermansen, but there was none. No punch, no parry, no save. Just indecision and a complete lack of intervention.

Unfortunately, this apparent hesitation has permeated Hermansen’s game recently and it’s hard not to conclude that he’s got the yips. There have been occasions when he has looked like little more than a bystander as goals have flown past him, sometimes appearing rooted to the spot or simply falling over rather than making a convincing attempt to save the ball.

The statistics are equally worrying. Based on the match figures we’ve examined, Hermansen has saved just 20% of the shots on target he has faced over West Ham’s last three Championship matches, conceding eight goals from ten attempts on target.

That’s an extraordinary return for a goalkeeper at any level, let alone one playing for a club with West Ham’s promotion ambitions. And while defenders must accept their share of the responsibility, the goalkeeper ultimately has to provide some resistance when opponents get a shot away.

The warning signs were already there before Cardiff, and his latest performance has only increased my concerns. I don’t know whether Hermansen is suffering from anything resembling the yips, but from watching him, I do wonder whether his confidence has deteriorated to the point where instinctive reactions are being replaced by hesitation.

This has become a huge problem, and one Scott Parker needs to address immediately. As things stand, I would have more confidence in either Alphonse Areola or Finlay Herrick than a goalkeeper who currently appears unable to make the saves West Ham desperately need.

Areola is an experienced international goalkeeper whom Parker already knows from their time together at Fulham. I thought he deserved his opportunity against Blackburn, and nothing I witnessed yesterday has changed my mind.

Hermansen’s performance was among the biggest disappointments in our Blackburn player ratings, and continuing to select him simply because he was previously considered first choice doesn’t make much sense when his performances have deteriorated so badly.

Clearly, there is a bigger issue to address in January, when West Ham will have another opportunity to examine their goalkeeping options. But we’ve only just entered November, and there are still two months and a hell of a lot of fixtures to negotiate before the transfer window opens.

That’s an awful lot of potential points to lose while waiting for a goalkeeper to rediscover his confidence. Parker has an international break in which to make some important decisions, and I would suggest the identity of his first-choice goalkeeper should be very near the top of that list.

#1995. Parker’s words prove he has so much more to offer than his predecessor | West Ham News

West Ham fans may have voiced their fury as the side slid one place further down the table after a poor run of results, but at least in Scott Parker the Hammers have a manager who understands how it really, really feels to have to witness that dross.

Unlike his predecessor Nuno Espírito Santo, Parker seems to have the ability to connect with the fan base and offer real empathy – along with hope that he will at least, work his nuts off to see a turnaround.

Nuno Espirito Santo was reduced to the same platitudes, the same apologies, but with the sense that it was just for the cameras and that he’d shrug his shoulders as soon as the interview was over, leaving someone else to fix the chaos in the dressing room and on the training pitch. West Ham’s training videos usually showed an assistant taking training, with Nuno either passive or absent entirely.

Even after a year Nuno struggled to convince fans that his ‘concern’ was heartfelt.

Parker has already surpassed his predecessor in terms of being ‘present’. Both his pronouncements and his actions – such as his first-game, half time team talk demonstrate his ability to wear his heart on his sleeve.

His words reported yesterday by footballleagueworld.co.uk do suggest, unlike his predecessor, that he’s genuinely hurting, along with the rest of us:

“Sounding somewhat hoarse after his team’s 2-1 defeat at Blackburn, Scott Parker spoke after the matchabout his disappointment at the result. Parker said that he’d talked about his team’s need to get a result from this match, even if it wasn’t playing the sort of football that he want his team to play.

He had sympathy for West Ham supporters, saying that he “wanted to get three points” for them, adding that, “What I can say is that I’m fully committed here, and I understand the pain, I understand where the fan base are.”

Parker added that he understands that the unhappiness of fans isn’t entirely a response to recent performances alone, saying that, “That’s not just this season, it’s come over a little bit of time.”

And he admitted that he was also hurting from this result: “I think everyone’s hurting here, and tonight I’m hurting because I understand that the only way we can change things is winning”

And it matters. Leadership doesn’t always yell, ( he’s done that too), sometimes it merely shows understanding and empathy whilst demanding better.

#1994. An open letter to Newcastle United fans

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

An open letter to my fellow Newcastle United fans – The 12th man.

‘We call ourselves the best supporters in the world. We wear our black and white stripes with pride. We sing about loyalty, passion, history and what it means to be a Geordie. We talk about St James’ Park being a fortress, about the noise, the atmosphere and the incredible connection between this club and its supporters.

Are we actually living up to the names we give ourselves?

Because, if I’m being honest, what we’ve witnessed at St James’ Park, particularly towards the back end of last season and continuing into this new chapter, has been difficult to watch. Not because of the football alone, but because of the attitude coming from the stands.

The atmosphere has, at times, become toxic. The groans, the negativity, the frustration, the booing at half-time and full-time. Players being written off before they’ve had a proper opportunity to settle. A new team being judged against the standards of a team that took years to build.

And I can’t help thinking that as Newcastle United fans we’ve lost sight of something incredibly important.

Look at what has happened at this football club. We’ve experienced significant change. A new manager, the loss of our club captain, the departure of experienced senior players and leaders, both on and off the pitch. The familiar faces, personalities and voices that helped shape the identity of this team have changed.

The dressing room has changed. The leadership has changed. The dynamics have changed. The team is evolving.

And yet, almost before this new group has had the opportunity to find its feet, we’ve been quick to turn on them.

Did we think a new manager would walk through the door, inherit a changing squad and everything would immediately click into place? That new partnerships, understanding, confidence and leadership would magically appear overnight?

Players need time to understand each other. New leaders need time to emerge. A manager needs time to implement his ideas. Confidence needs nurturing, not destroying.

And that last point is particularly important.

Imagine being a player walking out at St James’ Park, knowing that one misplaced pass, one poor decision or one disappointing half could be met with a chorus of groans or boos.

Imagine trying to build confidence in an unfamiliar team when the very people who are supposed to lift you are making you feel ten feet tall one minute and ten feet under the next.

We all want to win. We all want to see Newcastle competing at the highest level. Nobody is suggesting we should accept poor performances, abandon ambition or pretend everything is perfect when it isn’t.

We’re football supporters. We have every right to be frustrated, disappointed and demanding.

But there is a difference between demanding better and actively contributing to making things worse.

There is a difference between supporting a football club and only supporting it when things are going well.

This is Newcastle United. We know our history. We’ve experienced the highs, the lows, the heartbreak and the near misses. We’ve stood on the terraces through some truly difficult times. We know what loyalty means.

So why, now that the club is trying to build something, are we so quick to turn on the very people representing it?

The irony is that we constantly talk about the incredible atmosphere at St James’ Park. Opposition supporters talk about it. Players talk about it. Managers talk about it. It’s one of the things that makes Newcastle United special.

But that atmosphere isn’t created by the architecture, the pitch or the players alone.

We are the 12th man. Not a marketing slogan. Not something we sing about when we’re winning. Not something we switch on for the big European nights and switch off when a game isn’t going our way.

When the team is struggling, that’s when they need us most. When confidence is low, that’s when the noise should be loudest. When a new player makes a mistake, that’s when we should be getting behind him, not making him dread his next touch.

Imagine what it could do for a young player, a new signing or someone finding their feet in a different role to hear 52,000 people behind them rather than against them.

Imagine the confidence that could give a team still learning to play together.

We pride ourselves on being different. On being passionate, fiercely loyal and united behind our club. Well, perhaps it’s time we started showing it again.

Let’s stop comparing every new player with someone who has left. Let’s stop expecting a team in transition to perform like a settled side. Let’s give the manager and his players the opportunity to build relationships, develop an identity and find their rhythm.

And, above all, let’s remember that supporting Newcastle United isn’t conditional on the scoreline.

There will be poor performances. There will be mistakes. There will be frustrating afternoons, and Monday night catastrophes. There will be games when we leave St James’ Park wondering what on earth we’ve just watched.

But we should never allow frustration to become the defining feature of our support.

We have an opportunity here. A new chapter, a new group of players and a chance to build something together. The club has changed, and perhaps it’s time we changed our approach too.

The players have a responsibility to give everything for that shirt. The manager has a responsibility to get the best out of his squad. The board has a responsibility to take the club forward.

And we, the supporters, have a responsibility too.

Our job is to make St James’ Park a place opposition teams fear and our own players feel inspired.

So the next time we go through the turnstiles, let’s think about what we’re bringing into that stadium.

Let’s sing a little louder. Let’s get behind the players. Let’s lift them when they’re struggling. Let’s make some noise when things aren’t going our way.

Let’s be the supporters we constantly tell the rest of the world we are.

Because being the best fans in the world isn’t something you earn when your team wins.

It’s something you prove when they need you most.

We are Newcastle United. We are the Toon Army. We are the 12th man.

It’s about time we started acting like it.’

#1993. GdS: A combined salary less than Ramos’ – the story behind the Ferencvaros ‘miracle’

AC Milan’s opponents Ferencvaros are one of a few teams to have a perfect record in the Europa League, and their story is a fascinating one.

Ferencváros arrive at San Siro having won all three of their league phase games thus far. In addition to that, they are 20 unbeaten across all competitions and they will go top of their domestic league if they win their game in hand. La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) share some insight on the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Gonçalo Ramos’s gross salary €12.8m (€7m net including bonuses) is equivalent to the entire wage bill of Ferencváros. The combined salaries of the Hungarian club’s players total €11m.

Their highest earner is Naby Keïta, who accepted a contract worth just over €1.2m gross per season, seeking a career resurgence at the club with the largest payroll in the Hungarian league.

The Serbian midfielder Birmančević – formerly of Sparta Prague and Getafe, who arrived last summer – earns a slightly lower salary. Meanwhile, attacking midfielder Zachariassen earns around €700k and has scored three goals so far, as has Alphadjo Cissé.

In terms of wages, therefore, there is simply no comparison between the Rossoneri and Ferencváros. Yet, the Hungarians have won every match, while Milan have only three points. All the more reason not to take them lightly.

Gabor Kubatov has been on the board of Ferencváros since 2010, becoming president a year later. Under his leadership, the club has won eight Hungarian league titles. His personal history is quite unique: as a young man, he was a regular in ‘Sector 2’ – the section occupied by the ultras.

He later changed paths, and in 2006, he became a member of parliament, representing Fidesz, the party of Viktor Orbán. Despite his own background in the stands, his relationship with the Ferencváros ultras has not always been smooth.

In 2014, in an effort to combat violence and incidents of racism, Kubatov introduced a biometric identification system for stadium entry. A segment of the most ardent supporters responded by boycotting home matches, a protest that lasted for over three years.

An agreement was finally reached and the fans returned to the stands. With their support, Ferencváros went on to win seven consecutive league titles.

On 10 December 2017, a young Adam Nagy faced Milan while playing for Bologna. It didn’t go well: a 2-1 victory for the Rossoneri. Today, Nagy returns as a far more mature leader of his ‘miracle’ Ferencváros side.

Indeed, a significant portion of the Hungarian midfielder’s career has unfolded in Italy. He spent three years with the Rossoblù from 2016 to 2019 – following his initial breakthrough at Ferencváros – before returning to Italy in 2021 to join Pisa, having previously left to try his hand at Bristol City in England.

His most recent stint was with Spezia, which he departed this summer to return to his homeland. Yesterday, in a press conference, Rúben Amorim spoke very highly of him: “He is very skilled in the initial phase of build-up play.”

His ability to circulate the ball deep in his own half is his greatest strength. Conversely, he rarely ventures into the final third. The proof? Throughout all his years in Italy, he scored only one goal: against Verona in Serie A.

From the European champions Liverpool to Ferencvaros. Naby Keita – who will start on the bench tonight, hasn’t had the career he hoped for. Liverpool paid €65m to sign him from RB Leipzig in 2018, he won six more trophies in addition to the Champions League with Klopp’s English side.

In 2023, the Guinean midfielder moved to Werder Bremen, where he was left out of the squad after refusing to travel for the trip to Leverkusen because he wouldn’t have been a starter. Since January 2025, he has been at Ferencváros, who acquired him a year later.

Wearing a Liverpool shirt, Keïta has already beaten Milan at San Siro on 7 December 2021, a defeat that contributed to the Diavolo being eliminated in the group stage.

A less pleasant memory for Keïta involves his encounter with Luka Modrić when he came on in the final minutes of the 2022 Champions League final, which Liverpool lost to Real Madrid.
